# Heater core and A/C problems

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Remove the glove box, extract the storage box behind it, then use a multimeter to test for electrical faults. [t1485]

[Partial] Turn on cabin heater full blast while monitoring engine temperature at highway speeds. [t1880]

Start the engine and run the vehicle to check if the thermostat's temperature needle returns. [t1517]

## Procedure

2. Extract the storage box located behind the glove box by squeezing it out.

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1880] [Partial]</summary>

1. Turn on the cabin heater to full blast.
2. Monitor the engine temperature gauge while driving at highway speeds.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1517] [Partial]</summary>

2. [Partial] Run the vehicle for a while to allow it to warm up.

## Tips & gotchas

- If only replacing tubes, you do not need to pull everything out of the cabin. [t1485]
- [Partial] Use a multimeter to test for electrical faults if heat blows on specific settings like 3 and 4. [t1485]
- [Partial] Use this method when cruising above 65 mph and the fan clutch is declutched, causing airflow over radiator fins to decrease. [t1880]
- [Partial] If the gauge rises slowly but drops quickly once heat is applied, suspect restricted coolant flow or a failing fan clutch. [t1880]
- Check if the temperature needle returns to its original position. [t1517]
- Verify that cabin heat feels hotter after installation. [t1517]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Damaging the blower resistor during disassembly. [t1485]
